fix: load subsection sub-option defaults (#944)

fix(presets/newznab): set appropriate fallbacks for singleIp and showUnknown options

The Single-IP Mode toggle in Newznab's Zyclops health proxy subsection
has default: true. The boolean renderer falls back to the schema default
at display time (template-option.tsx:335), so the toggle correctly reads
ON when localValue is undefined. But the subsection modal seeds
localValue from the saved object only — sub-option defaults are never
merged in — so a user who never explicitly toggles the field saves
zyclopsHealthProxy without singleIp, and downstream the addon coerces
undefined → '0'.

Result for affected users: outbound proxy requests include single_ip=0
while the UI shows Single-IP Mode enabled. For an indexer-fronting
proxy where each request hits the upstream indexer from the user's
own IP, this is the difference between TOS-compliant and ban-risking
traffic.

Fix is in two parts:

1. Newznab preset (generateAddons): apply the schema defaults
   (singleIp ?? true, showUnknown ?? false) so existing user configs
   missing the field — saved before this fix, or saved without
   toggling — are corrected on next manifest generation. No user
   resave required. This pattern is already used in other presets
   (meteor.ts, flixStreams.ts).

2. TemplateOption subsection: seed the modal's localValue with
   sub-option defaults merged under the saved value. This prevents
   the same class of bug recurring for any future subsection that
   defines a `default: true` (or any non-undefined default) field.
   Saved values still win — only undefined sub-options pick up
   defaults.

fix(db): use pg_advisory_xact_lock to prevent migration lock leak (#976)

`driver.exec` routes each call through `pool.query()`, which checks
out a fresh pool connection per call. `pg_advisory_lock` and
`pg_advisory_unlock` therefore land on different connections; the
unlock no-ops (silently caught) while the original connection
returns to the pool still holding the session-level lock.

The orphaned holder is then recycled for normal app traffic. Its
old `xmin` snapshot prevents autovacuum from reclaiming any dead
tuples database-wide. Every subsequent replica boot queues behind
the orphan with no way out short of `pg_terminate_backend`. On
write-heavy deployments — for example v2.30's per-request
`UPDATE users SET accessed_at` path — the resulting bloat fills
the disk within a day or two.

Switch to `pg_advisory_xact_lock` inside `driver.tx()`. The lock
is auto-released by Postgres on COMMIT/ROLLBACK of the
transaction's pinned connection, so its lifecycle is tied to the
tx and cannot leak. Migrations themselves continue to run via the
outer pool exactly as before — only the lock acquisition needs to
be pinned.

fix: make RegexAccess/SelAccess cleanup safe to call before init (#980)

`RegexAccess.cleanup()` and `SelAccess.cleanup()` call
`this.manager.cleanup()`, where `manager` is a getter that lazily
constructs the SyncManager from `config.userLimits.regex` /
`config.userLimits.sel`. If shutdown runs before
`initialiseConfig()` has resolved — for example when SIGTERM
arrives during a slow startup, like a pod waiting on a slow DB
connection — the getter trips the settings-store's
`makeUninitialisedSectionProxy` guard:

  Error: appConfig.userLimits.regex was read at module-load time,
  before initialiseConfig() resolved. […]
      at get manager (regex-access.ts:31)
      at RegexAccess.cleanup (regex-access.ts:66)
      at shutdown (server.ts:185)

The shutdown handler turns a recoverable "killed during startup"
into an unhandled rejection. With multi-replica deployments, this
can crashloop pods that would otherwise just retry their boot.

Fix: skip cleanup when `_instance` was never created. Cleanup of a
never-initialised singleton is a no-op by definition; reading
config to *construct* the singleton just to clean it up is wrong.

fix(usenet): mint extension-less stream urls for cloudflare compatibility (#1070)

Cloudflare classifies requests by the URL path extension alone: a stream
URL ending in /<filename>.mkv is treated as a cacheable file type, so on
every cache miss (guaranteed, as the route sends no-store) the proxy
requests the entire file from origin and never forwards the client's
Range header. Every seek then costs a full-file pull, playback stalls,
and abandoned pulls pile up as orphaned full-file readers.

Dropping the filename segment makes Cloudflare treat the response as
dynamic and pass Range through verbatim. The route already accepts both
forms, so previously minted URLs keep working; players still receive the
real filename via Content-Disposition.

fix(torrent): lower the default get-torrent concurrency (#1193)

Results without an infohash have their .torrent downloaded to recover one, and
the default allowed 100 of those in flight per search. Nothing client-side
serialises them but indexers do — Prowlarr applies its per-indexer request
delay to downloads as well as searches — so past the first handful every
request spends its whole fetch timeout queued inside the indexer and is
abandoned after the indexer has already served it. On a such an indexer that
is a burst of ~100 downloads per search, none of them used.

Five keeps a rate-limited indexer inside the fetch timeout and is ample for
fast ones: .torrent files are small, and in the default lazy mode these
fetches are background work no request waits on.
